O.content: The title visibly reads "Decreasing Number of New Tourists in Town Z from 1880 to 1891".

B.text: If the chart title is an authoritative statement of the tourism trend and the word "Decreasing" is intended as the routing-relevant classification, then the decline-response route is appropriate.
B.conditions: Assumes the literal title overrides the contradictory plotted-line geometry; the chart supplies no rule resolving this conflict.

O.content: The title contains the word "Decreasing," while the blue line's endpoint at 1891 is higher on the page than its beginning at 1880.

B.text: If contradictory chart signals cannot be resolved because neither an authority hierarchy nor a routing threshold is supplied, then the trend cannot be classified reliably for escalation and routine monitoring is the conservative route.
B.conditions: Assumes routine monitoring is the appropriate default for unresolved evidence; this default is not stated in the task.

O.content: The blue line begins at the vertical alignment of the printed x-axis tick "1880".
The blue line ends at the vertical alignment of the printed x-axis tick "1891" and is higher on the page than its beginning at 1880.
The horizontal axis is visibly labeled "Year"; the vertical axis is visibly labeled "Number of New Tourists" and has printed values increasing upward from "0" to "4,000".

B.text: If the single plotted line is the dashboard's New tourists series, the horizontal axis encodes chronological year left-to-right, and higher vertical position maps to a larger number of new tourists using the upward-increasing y-axis, then a line ending higher than it begins indicates growth over the reviewed period. If the routing labels are intended to map a growth trend to growth planning, select the growth-planning route.
B.conditions: Assumes the plotted line, rather than the title text, is the authoritative encoding of Town Z new-tourist values and that a net increase warrants growth planning; no explicit routing policy is supplied.
